translations.literal: Grand Coordinator Weng Dali said: "Eastern Wu water conservancy, from Zhenze dredging the source to pour into the river, the Three Rivers guiding flow to enter the sea, while Suzhou's thirty-six creeks, Songjiang's eight confluences, and Piling's fourteen channels together regulate and release drought and flood.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Weng Dali reported, "Eastern Wu hydrology began with dredging Lake Tai's headwaters into the Yangtze and the Three Rivers' discharge to the sea; Suzhou's thirty-six creeks, Songjiang's eight confluences, and Piling's fourteen channels together balanced drought and flood.

sentences.zh: 近因倭寇衝突，汊港之交，率多釘柵築堤以為捍禦，因致水流停瀦，淤滓日積。

translations.literal: Recently because of wokou clashes, at the junctions of branch harbors, mostly they nailed palisades and built dikes for defense, thereby causing water flow to halt and impound and silt dregs daily to accumulate.
translations.idiomatic: Lately, wokou raids had led people to spike harbors and throw up dikes for defense, so currents stalled, silt piled up daily,

sentences.zh: 管道之間，仰高成阜。

translations.literal: Between conduit channels, looking up they became mounds.
translations.idiomatic: and channel beds rose into embankments.

sentences.zh: 且具區湖泖，並水而居者雜蒔茭蘆，積泥成蕩，民間又多自起圩岸。

translations.literal: Moreover at Juqu lake marshes, those dwelling by water miscellaneously planted reed and rush, accumulated mud into shallows, and among the people many themselves raised polder dikes.
translations.idiomatic: Around Lake Tai and the marshes, waterside residents planted reeds and rushes until mud piled into shallows, while countless private polder dikes sprang up.

sentences.zh: 上流日微，水勢日殺。

translations.literal: Upstream daily grew slight, water momentum daily weakened.
translations.idiomatic: Upstream flow dwindled daily and hydraulic force weakened.

sentences.zh: 黃浦、婁江之水又為舟師所居，下流亦淤。

translations.literal: Huangpu and Lou River waters again were occupied by boat troops; downstream also silted.
translations.idiomatic: The Huangpu and Lou River were choked by naval moorings, and downstream silted as well.

sentences.zh: 海潮無力，水利難興，民田漸磽。

translations.literal: Sea tide without strength, water conservancy hard to rise, people's fields gradually barren.
translations.idiomatic: With the tides too weak to scour the channels, waterworks languished and farmland turned ever stonier.

sentences.zh: 宜於吳淞、白茆、七浦等處造成石閘，啟閉以時。

translations.literal: It is fitting at Wusong, Baimao, Qipu, and other places to build stone sluices, opening and closing according to season.
translations.idiomatic: Stone sluice gates should be built at Wusong, Baimao, Qipu, and the like, opened and closed according to season.

sentences.zh: 挑鎮江、常州漕河深廣，使輸挽無阻，公私之利也。

translations.literal: Dredge Zhenjiang and Changzhou grain-transport rivers deep and broad, so transport hauling has no obstruction—public and private benefit.
translations.idiomatic: The grain canals at Zhenjiang and Changzhou should be dredged deep and wide so transport would run unimpeded—a gain for state and subject alike.

sentences.zh: 」詔可。

translations.literal: " An edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: " Approved.

sentences.zh: 四十二年，給事中張憲臣言：「蘇、鬆、常、嘉、湖五郡水患疊見。

translations.literal: In the forty-second year, supervising secretary Zhang Xianchen said: "The five prefectures Suzhou, Song, Chang, Jia, and Hu repeatedly show water calamity.
translations.idiomatic: In year 42, Supervising Secretary Zhang Xianchen reported, "Floods had struck Suzhou, Songjiang, Changzhou, Jiaxing, and Huzhou in succession.

sentences.zh: 請浚支河，通潮水；

translations.literal: Ask to dredge branch rivers, connect tidal water;
translations.idiomatic: He asked that branch channels be dredged and tidal flow restored;

sentences.zh: 築圩岸，禦湍流。

translations.literal: build polder dikes, defend against turbulent flow.
translations.idiomatic: and polder dikes built to beat back surging currents.

sentences.zh: 其白茆港、劉家河、七浦、楊林及凡河渠河蕩壅淤沮洳者，悉宜疏導。

translations.literal: Baimao Port, Liujia River, Qipu, Yanglin, and all rivers, channels, and river marshes blocked, silted, oozy, and waterlogged—altogether should be dredged and guided.
translations.idiomatic: Baimao Harbor, the Liujia River, Qipu, Yanglin, and every choked ditch and marsh should be cleared.

sentences.zh: 」帝以江南久苦倭患，民不宜重勞，令酌浚支河而已。

translations.literal: " The emperor, because Jiangnan long suffered wokou harm and the people should not be heavily labored, ordered to consider dredging branch rivers only.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor, mindful that Jiangnan had long endured wokou raids and the people could bear no heavy labor, authorized dredging of branch channels alone.

sentences.zh: 四十五年，參政淩雲翼請專設御史督蘇、鬆水利。

translations.literal: In the forty-fifth year, vice commissioner Ling Yunyi asked to specially establish a censor to supervise Suzhou-Song water conservancy.
translations.idiomatic: In year 45, Vice Commissioner Ling Yunyi asked for a dedicated censor to oversee Suzhou-Songjiang hydrology.

sentences.zh: 詔巡鹽御史兼之。

translations.literal: An edict: the salt-circuit censor additionally takes it.
translations.idiomatic: The salt-route censor was ordered to take on the duty as well.

sentences.zh: 隆慶三年，開湖廣竹筒河以泄漢江。

translations.literal: In the third year of Longqing, open Huguang Bamboo-tube River to drain the Han River.
translations.idiomatic: Longqing 3: the Bamboo-tube River in Huguang was opened to relieve the Han River.

sentences.zh: 巡撫都御史海瑞疏吳淞江下流上海淤地萬四千丈有奇。

translations.literal: Grand Coordinator Hai Rui memorialized that the lower reach of the Wusong River at Shanghai had silt land of more than fourteen thousand zhang odd.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Coordinator Hai Rui reported more than fourteen thousand zhang of silt along the lower Wusong at Shanghai.

sentences.zh: 江面舊三十丈，增開十五丈，自黃渡至宋家橋長八十里。

translations.literal: The river surface was formerly thirty zhang; the opening was widened by fifteen zhang, from Huangdu to Songjia Bridge a length of eighty li.
translations.idiomatic: The channel, formerly thirty zhang wide, was widened by fifteen zhang from Huangdu to Songjia Bridge—a stretch of eighty li.

sentences.zh: 明年春，瑞言：「三吳入海之道，南止吳淞，北止白茆，中止劉河。

translations.literal: The next spring, Rui said: "The Three Wu routes to the sea: south ends at Wusong, north ends at Baimao, center ends at Liuhe.
translations.idiomatic: The following spring Hai Rui wrote, "The Three Wu had three outlets to the sea: Wusong in the south, Baimao in the north, and Liuhe in the middle.

sentences.zh: 劉河通達無滯，吳淞方在挑疏。

translations.literal: Liuhe connects without delay; Wusong is just in dredging.
translations.idiomatic: Liuhe was open throughout; Wusong was still being dredged.

sentences.zh: 土人請開白茆，計浚五千餘丈，役夫百六十四萬餘。

translations.literal: Local people asked to open Baimao; the plan dredged more than five thousand zhang, laborers more than 1.64 million.
translations.idiomatic: Locals petitioned to open Baimao—some five thousand zhang of dredging and more than 1.64 million labor-days.

sentences.zh: 」又言：「吳淞役垂竣，惟東西二壩未開。

translations.literal: " He also said: "The Wusong project is nearly complete; only the east and west two dams are not opened.
translations.idiomatic: " He added that the Wusong work was nearly done but the eastern and western dams remained closed.

sentences.zh: 父老皆言崑山夏駕口、吳江長橋、長洲寶帶橋、吳縣胥口及凡可通流下吳淞者，逐一挑畢，方可開壩。

translations.literal: The elders all said that Kunshan Xiadjiakou, Wujiang Chang Bridge, Changzhou Baodai Bridge, Wuxian Xukou, and all that could connect flow down to Wusong must be dredged one by one to completion before the dams could be opened.
translations.idiomatic: Elders insisted that Xiadjiakou in Kunshan, Chang Bridge in Wujiang, Baodai Bridge in Changzhou, Xukou in Wuxian, and every outlet feeding the Wusong be cleared first—only then could the dams be opened.

sentences.zh: 」並從之。

translations.literal: All were followed.
translations.idiomatic: All was approved.

sentences.zh: 是年築海鹽海塘。

translations.literal: That year the Haiyan seadike was built.
translations.idiomatic: That year the Haiyan seadike was built.

sentences.zh: 越四年，從巡撫侍郎徐栻議，復開海鹽秦駐山，南至澉浦舊河。

translations.literal: Four years on, following Vice Commissioner Xu Zhi's plan, reopen Haiyan Qinzhushan, south to the old river at Ganpu.
translations.idiomatic: Four years later, on Vice Commissioner Xu Zhi's advice, the channel from Qinzhushan in Haiyan south to the old Ganpu river was reopened.

sentences.zh: 萬曆二年，築荊州採穴，承天泗港、謝家灣諸決堤口。

translations.literal: In the second year of Wanli, build Jingzhou Caiyue, Chengtian Sigang, Xiejiawan, and other breached dike mouths.
translations.idiomatic: Wanli 2: breach closures were built at Jingzhou's Caiyue, Chengtian's Sigang, Xiejiawan, and elsewhere.

sentences.zh: 復築荊、嶽等府及鬆滋諸縣老垸堤。

translations.literal: Again build the old polder dikes of Jing, Yue, and other prefectures and Songzi and other counties.
translations.idiomatic: Old polder dikes were also restored in Jingzhou, Yuezhou, and other prefectures and in Songzi and neighboring counties.

sentences.zh: 四年，巡撫都御史宋儀望言：「三吳水勢，東南自嘉、秀沿海而北，皆趨松江，循黃浦入海；

translations.literal: In the fourth year, Grand Coordinator Song Yiwang said: "Three Wu water momentum: southeast from Jia and Xiu along the coast northward all trend toward Songjiang, following the Huangpu to enter the sea;
translations.idiomatic: In year 4, Grand Coordinator Song Yiwang wrote, "In the Three Wu, waters from Jiaxing and Xiuzhou along the coast trend north to Songjiang and out through the Huangpu;

sentences.zh: 西北自常、鎮沿江而東，皆趨江陰、常熟。

translations.literal: northwest from Chang and Zhen along the river eastward all trend toward Jiangyin and Changshu.
translations.idiomatic: from Changzhou and Zhenjiang along the Yangtze they trend east toward Jiangyin and Changshu.

sentences.zh: 其中太湖瀦蓄，匯為巨浸，流注龐山、瀆墅、澱山、三泖，陽城諸湖。

translations.literal: Within, Tai Lake stores and gathers into a great flood, flowing into Pangshan, Dushu, Dianshan, the Three Mo, Yangcheng, and other lakes.
translations.idiomatic: Tai Lake impounds the surplus into a vast sheet that feeds Pangshan, Dushu, Dianshan, the Three Mo, Yangcheng, and other lakes.

sentences.zh: 乃開浦引湖，北經常熟七浦、白茆諸港入於江，東北經崑山、太倉穿劉家河，東南通吳淞江、黃浦，各入於海。

translations.literal: Then open creeks to draw the lakes: north through Changshu's Qipu, Baimao, and other harbors into the river; northeast through Kunshan and Taicang via the Liujia River; southeast through the Wusong River and Huangpu—each entering the sea.
translations.idiomatic: Creeks draw the lakes north through Changshu's Qipu and Baimao into the Yangtze, northeast through Kunshan and Taicang via the Liujia River, and southeast through the Wusong and Huangpu to the sea.

sentences.zh: 諸水聯絡，四面環護，中如仰盂。

translations.literal: The waters link together, encircled on four sides, the center like an up-turned bowl.
translations.idiomatic: The waters interlock, ringed on every side, the basin like an upturned bowl.

sentences.zh: 杭、嘉湖、常、鎮勢繞四隅，蘇州居中，松江為諸水所受，最居下。

translations.literal: Hang, Jia, Hu, Chang, and Zhen's momentum surrounds the four corners; Suzhou lies in the center; Songjiang receives all the waters and is lowest.
translations.idiomatic: Hangzhou, Jiaxing, Huzhou, Changzhou, and Zhenjiang rim the four corners; Suzhou sits in the middle; Songjiang, lowest of all, receives every stream.

sentences.zh: 乞專設水利僉事以裨國計。

translations.literal: We ask to specially establish a water conservancy associate to benefit state accounts.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that a dedicated hydrology intendant be appointed to strengthen state revenue.

sentences.zh: 」部議遣御史董之。

translations.literal: " The ministry discussed dispatching a censor to oversee it.
translations.idiomatic: " The ministry agreed to send a censor to supervise.

sentences.zh: 六年，巡撫都御史胡執禮請先浚吳淞江長橋、黃浦。

translations.literal: In the sixth year, Grand Coordinator Hu Zhili asked first to dredge the Wusong River at Chang Bridge and the Huangpu.
translations.idiomatic: In year 6, Grand Coordinator Hu Zhili asked that the Wusong at Chang Bridge and the Huangpu be dredged first.

sentences.zh: 先是，巡按御史林應訓言：

translations.literal: Earlier, investigating censor Lin Yingxun said:
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Investigating Censor Lin Yingxun had reported:

sentences.zh: 「蘇、鬆水利在開吳淞江中段，以通入海之勢。

translations.literal: "Suzhou-Song water conservancy lies in opening the middle section of the Wusong River to connect momentum to the sea.
translations.idiomatic: "Suzhou-Songjiang hydrology depends on opening the middle reach of the Wusong so the lake may pour to the sea.

sentences.zh: 太湖入海，其道有三：東北由劉河，即古婁江故道；

translations.literal: Tai Lake enters the sea; its routes have three: northeast by Liuhe, the ancient Lou River's old course;
translations.idiomatic: Tai Lake has three outlets: northeast via Liuhe, the old course of the Lou River;

sentences.zh: 東南由大黃浦，即古東江遺意；

translations.literal: southeast by the Great Huangpu, the vestige of the ancient Eastern River;
translations.idiomatic: southeast via the Great Huangpu, heir to the ancient Eastern River;

sentences.zh: 其中為吳淞江，經崑山、嘉定、青浦、上海，乃太湖正脈。

translations.literal: in the center the Wusong River, passing Kunshan, Jiading, Qingpu, and Shanghai—Tai Lake's main artery.
translations.idiomatic: and between them the Wusong through Kunshan, Jiading, Qingpu, and Shanghai—the lake's main artery.

sentences.zh: 今劉河、黃浦皆通，而中江獨塞者，蓋江流與海潮遇，海潮渾濁，賴江水迅滌之。

translations.literal: Now Liuhe and Huangpu are all open, but the center river alone is blocked, because river flow meets sea tide; sea tide is turbid, relying on river water swift to wash it.
translations.idiomatic: Liuhe and the Huangpu stay clear, yet the middle channel alone silts up: where river meets tide the seawater is muddy and only a swift freshwater current can scour it.

sentences.zh: 劉河獨受巴、陽諸湖，又有新洋江、夏駕浦從旁以注；

translations.literal: Liuhe alone receives the Ba and Yang lakes, and also has the Xinyang River and Xiadjiapu pouring in from the side;
translations.idiomatic: Liuhe draws the Ba and Yang lakes and gains the Xinyang River and Xiadjiapu besides;

sentences.zh: 大黃浦總會杭、嘉之水，又有澱山、泖蕩從上而灌。

translations.literal: the Great Huangpu gathers Hang and Jia's waters, and also has Dianshan and Mo marshes flooding down from above.
translations.idiomatic: the Great Huangpu collects Hangzhou and Jiaxing and is fed from above by Dianshan and the Mo marshes.

sentences.zh: 是以流皆清駛，足以敵潮，不能淤也。

translations.literal: Therefore the flows are all clear and swift, sufficient to resist the tide and cannot silt.
translations.idiomatic: Their currents run clear and fast enough to beat the tide and resist silting.

sentences.zh: 惟吳淞江源出長橋、石塘下，經龐山、九里二湖而入。

translations.literal: Only the Wusong River's source exits below Chang Bridge and Shitang, passing the two lakes Pangshan and Jiuli to enter.
translations.idiomatic: The Wusong alone rises below Chang Bridge and Shitang and passes through Pangshan and Jiuli lakes.

sentences.zh: 今長橋、石塘已堙，龐山、九里復為灘漲，其來已微。

translations.literal: Now Chang Bridge and Shitang are buried; Pangshan and Jiuli again are beach swells; its incoming flow is already slight.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Bridge and Shitang are choked; Pangshan and Jiuli have silted into shallows; the inflow is feeble.

sentences.zh: 又有新洋江、夏駕浦掣其水以入劉河，勢乃益弱，不能勝海潮洶湧之勢而滌濁渾之流，日積月累，淤塞僅留一線。

translations.literal: Also the Xinyang River and Xiadjiapu draw off its water into Liuhe; momentum then grows weaker still, unable to overcome the sea tide's surging force to wash the turbid muddy flow; day by day and month by month it accumulates until blockage leaves only a thread.
translations.idiomatic: The Xinyang and Xiadjiapu further divert water into Liuhe, weakening the current until it cannot scour the muddy tide; month by month the channel shrank to a thread.

sentences.zh: 水失故道，時致淫濫。

translations.literal: Water lost its old course and at times caused excessive flooding.
translations.idiomatic: Water lost its proper course and floods broke out repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 支河小港，亦復壅滯。

translations.literal: Branch rivers and small harbors also again were blocked and stagnant.
translations.idiomatic: Branch channels and creeks silted up as well.

sentences.zh: 舊熟之田，半成荒畝。

translations.literal: Fields once ripe were half become waste mu.
translations.idiomatic: Half the once-fertile fields lay waste.

sentences.zh: 前都御史海瑞力破羣議，挑自上海江口宋家橋至嘉定艾祁八十里，幸尚通流。

translations.literal: Former minister Hai Rui forcefully broke group opinion and dredged from Shanghai river mouth Songjia Bridge to Jiading Aiqi eighty li; fortunately flow still connects.
translations.idiomatic: Former minister Hai Rui had defied widespread opposition and dredged eighty li from Songjia Bridge at Shanghai to Aiqi in Jiading; that stretch still flowed.

sentences.zh: 自艾祁至崑山慢水港六十餘里，則俱漲灘，急宜開浚，計淺九千五百餘丈，闊二十丈。

translations.literal: From Aiqi to Kunshan Manshui Harbor more than sixty li, then all are swollen beaches; urgently should be opened and dredged—planned shallow stretches more than nine thousand five hundred zhang, breadth twenty zhang.
translations.idiomatic: From Aiqi to Manshui Harbor in Kunshan—sixty-odd li of shoals—must be opened at once: some nine thousand five hundred zhang to deepen to twenty zhang wide.

sentences.zh: 此江一開，太湖直入於海，濱江諸渠得以引流灌田，青浦積荒之區俱可開墾成熟矣。」

translations.literal: Once this river is opened, Tai Lake will enter the sea directly; riverside channels can draw flow to irrigate fields, and Qingpu's accumulated waste districts all can be opened, reclaimed, and brought to ripeness."
translations.idiomatic: Open that reach and Tai Lake would pour straight to the sea; coastal channels could irrigate the fields, and Qingpu's long-fallow land could be brought back under the plow."

sentences.zh: 並從之。

translations.literal: All were followed.
translations.idiomatic: All was approved.

sentences.zh: 至是，工成。

translations.literal: By this time the work was completed.
translations.idiomatic: The work was finished.

sentences.zh: 應訓又言：

translations.literal: Yingxun again said:
translations.idiomatic: Lin Yingxun added:

sentences.zh: 「吳江縣治居太湖正東，湖水由此下吳淞達海。

translations.literal: "Wujiang county seat lies due east of Tai Lake; lake water from here descends the Wusong to reach the sea.
translations.idiomatic: "Wujiang's seat lies directly east of Tai Lake; its waters descend the Wusong to the sea.

sentences.zh: 宋時運道所經，畏風阻險，乃建長橋、石塘以通牽挽。

translations.literal: In Song times the transport route passed here; fearing wind obstruction and danger, they then built Chang Bridge and Shitang to connect towing.
translations.idiomatic: When the Song grain route passed this way, fear of wind and shoals led them to build Chang Bridge and Shitang for towing haulers.

sentences.zh: 長橋百三十丈，為洞六十有二。

translations.literal: Chang Bridge is one hundred thirty zhang long, with sixty-two culvert openings.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Bridge spans one hundred thirty zhang and has sixty-two arch openings.

sentences.zh: 石塘小則有竇，大則有橋，內外浦涇縱橫貫穿，皆為泄水計也。

translations.literal: At Shitang, where the works are small there are culverts and where large there are bridges; inner and outer creeks and canals crisscross in every direction—all planned for draining water.
translations.idiomatic: Along Shitang, small sections have sluice openings and large ones have bridges; creeks and canals crisscross within and without, all designed to let water off.

sentences.zh: 石塘涇竇半淤，長橋內外俱圮，僅一二洞門通水。

translations.literal: Shitang's canals and culverts are half silted; inside and outside Chang Bridge all are collapsed; only one or two culvert gates pass water.
translations.idiomatic: Shitang's channels and culverts are half choked with silt; Chang Bridge is ruined on both sides, and only one or two arch openings still carry water.

sentences.zh: 若不疏浚，雖開吳淞下流，終無益也。

translations.literal: If not dredged and cleared, although the lower Wusong is opened, in the end there will be no benefit.
translations.idiomatic: Without dredging here, opening the lower Wusong would do no good in the end.

sentences.zh: 宜開龐山湖口，由長橋抵吳家港。

translations.literal: It is fitting to open Pangshan Lake's mouth, from Chang Bridge reaching Wujia Harbor.
translations.idiomatic: Pangshan Lake's outlet should be opened, with a channel from Chang Bridge to Wujia Harbor.

sentences.zh: 則湖有所泄，江有所歸，源盛流長，為利大矣。

translations.literal: Then the lake will have an outlet, the river will have a destination, sources full and flows long—the benefit will be great indeed.
translations.idiomatic: The lake would drain, the river would have a proper course, sources would run strong and long—and the benefit would be immense.

sentences.zh: 松江大黃浦西南受杭、嘉之水，西北受氵殿、泖諸蕩之水，總會於浦，而秀州塘、山涇港諸處實黃浦來源也。

translations.literal: Songjiang's Great Huangpu on the southwest receives Hangzhou and Jiaxing waters, on the northwest receives Dianshan, Mo, and various lagoon waters, all gathering in the pu; but Xiuzhou Canal, Shanjing Harbor, and such places are truly Huangpu's sources.
translations.idiomatic: Songjiang's Great Huangpu takes in Hangzhou and Jiaxing waters from the southwest and Dianshan, Mo, and other lagoon waters from the northwest, all gathering in the channel; yet Xiuzhou Canal, Shanjing Harbor, and the like are the Huangpu's true headwaters.

sentences.zh: 氵殿山湖入黃浦道漸多淤淺，宜為疏瀹。

translations.literal: Dianshan Lake's route into Huangpu is gradually more silted and shallow; it should be dredged and cleared.
translations.idiomatic: The channel from Dianshan Lake into the Huangpu is growing shallow with silt and should be dredged.

sentences.zh: 而自黃浦、橫澇、洙涇，經秀州塘入南泖，至山涇港等處，萬四千餘丈，待浚尤急。

translations.literal: And from Huangpu, Henglao, and Zhujing, passing Xiuzhou Canal entering South Mo, reaching Shanjing Harbor and other places, more than fourteen thousand zhang—awaiting dredging especially urgent.
translations.idiomatic: From the Huangpu, Henglao, and Zhujing, through Xiuzhou Canal into the South Mo, down to Shanjing Harbor—a stretch of more than fourteen thousand zhang urgently needing dredging.

sentences.zh: 他如蘇之茜涇、楊林、白茆、七浦諸港，鬆之蒲匯、官紹諸塘，常、鎮之澡港、九曲諸河，並宜設法開導，次第修舉。」

translations.literal: Others such as Suzhou's Qianjing, Yanglin, Baimao, and Qipu various harbors; Songjiang's Puhui and Guanshao various canals; Changzhou and Zhenjiang's Zaogang and Jiuqu various rivers—all should by devised means be opened and guided, in order repaired and carried out."
translations.idiomatic: The same holds for Suzhou's Qianjing, Yanglin, Baimao, and Qipu harbors; Songjiang's Puhui and Guanshao canals; and Changzhou and Zhenjiang's Zaogang and Jiuqu rivers—each should be opened by proper methods and repaired in turn."

sentences.zh: 八年，又言：「蘇、鬆諸郡幹河支港凡數百，大則泄水入海，次則通湖達江，小則引流灌田。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, again said: "Suzhou and Songjiang various prefectures' trunk rivers and branch harbors number several hundred; large ones drain water to the sea, secondary ones connect lakes and reach rivers, small ones draw flow to irrigate fields.
translations.idiomatic: In year eight he again reported, "Suzhou and Songjiang have hundreds of trunk channels and branch waterways—large ones discharge to the sea, middling ones link lakes to rivers, small ones carry water to the fields.

sentences.zh: 今吳淞江、白茆塘、秀州塘、蒲匯塘、孟瀆河、舜河、青暘港俱已告成，支河數十，宜盡開浚。

translations.literal: Now Wusong River, Baimao Canal, Xiuzhou Canal, Puhui Canal, Mengdu River, Shun River, and Qingyang Harbor all have been reported completed; branch rivers several tens—it is fitting all be opened and dredged.
translations.idiomatic: The Wusong, Baimao Canal, Xiuzhou Canal, Puhui Canal, Mengdu River, Shun River, and Qingyang Harbor are now finished; dozens of branch streams should all be dredged open.

sentences.zh: 」俱從其請。

translations.literal: " All followed his request.
translations.idiomatic: All was approved.

sentences.zh: 久之，用儀望議，特設蘇、鬆水利副使，以許應逵領之。

translations.literal: After a long time, adopting Yi Wang's proposal, a special post of Suzhou-Songjiang hydraulic vice commissioner was established, with Xu Yingkui to head it.
translations.idiomatic: Later, on Yi Wang's recommendation, a special vice commissioner for Suzhou and Songjiang hydraulic works was created, with Xu Yingkui in charge.

sentences.zh: 乃浚吳淞八十餘晨，築塘九十餘處，開新河百二十三道，浚內河百三十九道，築上海李家洪老鴉嘴海岸十八里，發帑金二十萬。

translations.literal: Thereupon he dredged the Wusong more than eighty zhang, built embankments at more than ninety places, opened one hundred twenty-three new river channels, dredged one hundred thirty-nine inner rivers, built eighteen li of coast at Shanghai's Lijiahong and Laoyazui, and issued two hundred thousand taels from the treasury.
translations.idiomatic: He dredged more than eighty zhang of the Wusong, built embankments at ninety-plus sites, cut one hundred twenty-three new channels and cleared one hundred thirty-nine inner waterways, raised eighteen li of coast at Shanghai's Lijiahong and Laoyazui, and disbursed two hundred thousand taels from the treasury.

sentences.zh: 應逵以其半訖工。

translations.literal: Yingkui with half of it completed the work.
translations.idiomatic: Yingkui brought the work to completion with half that sum.

sentences.zh: 三十七、八年間，霪雨浸溢，水患日熾。

translations.literal: In the thirty-seventh and thirty-eighth years, incessant rain overflowed and spread; water disasters daily grew fierce.
translations.idiomatic: In years thirty-seven and thirty-eight, unending rain brought floods, and the water crisis grew worse by the day.

sentences.zh: 越數年，給事中歸子顧言：「宋時，吳淞江闊九里。

translations.literal: After several years, supervising secretary Gui Ziguan said: "In Song times, the Wusong River was nine li wide.
translations.idiomatic: Several years on, supervising secretary Gui Ziguan memorialized, "Under the Song the Wusong was nine li wide.

sentences.zh: 元末淤塞。

translations.literal: At Yuan's end it silted and blocked.
translations.idiomatic: By the late Yuan it had silted shut.

sentences.zh: 正統間，周忱立表江心，疏而浚之。

translations.literal: In the Zhengtong era, Zhou Chen set a gauge at the river's center, dredged and cleared it.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhengtong reign Zhou Chen set a gauge midstream and dredged it clear.

sentences.zh: 崔恭、徐貫、李充嗣、海瑞相繼浚者凡五，迄今四十餘年，廢而不講。

translations.literal: Cui Gong, Xu Guan, Li Chongsi, and Hai Rui in succession dredged—five in all; from then until now forty-odd years, abandoned and not discussed.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Gong, Xu Guan, Li Chongsi, and Hai Rui undertook dredging in turn—five efforts in all—yet for more than forty years since, the work has lain neglected.

sentences.zh: 宜使江闊水駛，塘浦支河分流四達。

translations.literal: It is fitting to make the river wide and water swift; embankment creeks and branch rivers divide flow in four directions.
translations.idiomatic: The river should be widened and the current quickened, with canal embankments and branch streams branching flow in every direction.

sentences.zh: 」疏入留中。

translations.literal: " The memorial entered and was kept at court.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was filed and held over at court.

sentences.zh: 巡按御史薛貞復請行之，下部議而未行。

translations.literal: Investigating censor Xue Zhen again requested it be carried out; sent down to ministries for discussion but not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Investigating censor Xue Zhen petitioned again for implementation; the ministries debated it, but nothing was done.

sentences.zh: 至天啟中，巡撫都御史周起元復請浚吳淞、白茆。

translations.literal: Reaching the Tianqi era, grand coordinator Zhou Qiyuan again requested dredging the Wusong and Baimao.
translations.idiomatic: In the Tianqi reign, grand coordinator Zhou Qiyuan again urged dredging the Wusong and Baimao.

sentences.zh: 崇禎初，員外郎蔡懋德、巡撫都御史李待問皆以為請。

translations.literal: At Chongzhen's beginning, vice director Cai Maode and grand coordinator Li Daiwen all took it as a request.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Chongzhen, vice director Cai Maode and grand coordinator Li Daiwen both pressed the same plea.

sentences.zh: 久之，巡撫都御史張國維請疏吳江長橋七十二谼及九里、石塘諸洞。

translations.literal: After a long time, grand coordinator Zhang Guowei requested dredging Wujiang Chang Bridge's seventy-two gorges and the culverts at Jiuli and Shitang.
translations.idiomatic: Later, grand coordinator Zhang Guowei asked to clear Wujiang's seventy-two gorges at Chang Bridge plus the culverts at Jiuli and Shitang.

sentences.zh: 御史李謨復請浚吳淞、白茆。

translations.literal: Censor Li Mo again requested dredging the Wusong and Baimao.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Li Mo again urged dredging the Wusong and Baimao.

sentences.zh: 俱下部議，未能行也。

translations.literal: All sent down to ministries for discussion; could not be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Each proposal went to the ministries for debate, and none could be implemented.

sentences.zh: 十年，增築雄縣橫堤八里，禦滹沱暴漲。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, additionally built Xiongxian transverse dike eight li, to defend against Hutuo violent rise.
translations.idiomatic: In year ten, Xiongxian's transverse dike was extended eight li to hold back the Hutuo in flood.

sentences.zh: 十三年，以尚寶少卿徐貞明兼御史，領墾田使。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, Junior Chamberlain for Imperial Insignia Xu Zhenming was concurrently made censor, leading land-reclamation commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In year thirteen Xu Zhenming, Junior Chamberlain for Imperial Insignia, was also appointed investigating censor and put in charge of land reclamation.

sentences.zh: 貞明為給事中，嘗請興西北水利如南人圩田之制，引水成田。

translations.literal: Zhenming as supervising secretary once requested promoting northwest water conservancy like southerners' polder-field system, drawing water to form fields.
translations.idiomatic: While still a supervising secretary, Zhenming had urged developing northwestern irrigation on the southern polder model, channeling water to make fields.

sentences.zh: 工部覆議：「畿輔諸郡邑，以上流十五河之水泄於貓兒一灣，海口又極束隘，故所在橫流。

translations.literal: Ministry of Works replied: "Capital-region various prefectures and counties—above, fifteen rivers' waters discharge at Maor Bay alone; the estuary moreover is extremely narrow and blocked, hence everywhere crossflow.
translations.idiomatic: The Ministry of Works replied, "In the metropolitan region, the waters of fifteen upstream rivers all empty into Maor Bay alone, while the estuary is desperately narrow—so floods spread everywhere.

sentences.zh: 必多開支河，挑浚海口，而後水勢可平，疏浚可施。

translations.literal: Must open many branch rivers, dredge the estuary, and afterward water force can be leveled, dredging can be applied.
translations.idiomatic: Branch channels must be opened and the estuary dredged before the waters can level off and ordinary dredging can succeed.

sentences.zh: 然役大費繁，而今以民勞財匱，方務省事，請罷其議。

translations.literal: Yet the labor is great and costs manifold; and now with the people weary and treasury depleted, just then pursuing economy in affairs—request to abandon this proposal.
translations.idiomatic: But the labor would be vast and costly, and with the people exhausted and the treasury bare the court was bent on retrenchment—so they asked that the plan be dropped.

sentences.zh: 」乃已。

translations.literal: " Thereupon it ceased.
translations.idiomatic: And so it ended.

sentences.zh: 後貞明謫官，著《潞水客譚》一書，論水利當興者十四條。

translations.literal: Later Zhenming was demoted in office; he wrote the book Visitor's Talk on Lu River Water, discussing water conservancy that should be promoted—fourteen articles.
translations.idiomatic: Later, after Zhenming was demoted, he wrote *Visitor's Talk on Lu River Water*, setting out fourteen proposals for waterworks that ought to be revived.

sentences.zh: 時巡撫張國彥、副使顧養謙方開水利於薊、永有效，於是給事中王敬民薦貞明，特召還，賜敕勘水利。

translations.literal: At the time grand coordinator Zhang Guoyan and vice commissioner Gu Yangqian were just opening water conservancy in Ji and Yong with effect; thereupon supervising secretary Wang Jingmin recommended Zhenming; he was specially recalled, granted imperial edict to survey water conservancy.
translations.idiomatic: Grand coordinator Zhang Guoyan and vice commissioner Gu Yangqian were then opening works in Ji and Yong with good effect; supervising secretary Wang Jingmin recommended Zhenming, who was specially recalled and charged by edict to survey hydraulic works.

sentences.zh: 貞明乃先治京東州邑，如密雲燕樂莊，平谷水峪寺、龍家務莊，三河塘會莊、順慶屯地。

translations.literal: Zhenming then first managed eastern capital prefectures and districts, such as Miyun's Yanle Manor, Pinggu's Shuiyu Temple and Longjiawu Manor, Sanhe's Tanghui Manor and Shunqing garrison lands.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenming began in the eastern capital districts—Miyun's Yanle Manor; Pinggu's Shuiyu Temple and Longjiawu Manor; Sanhe's Tanghui Manor and Shunqing garrison lands.

sentences.zh: 薊州城北黃厓營，城西白馬泉、鎮國莊，城東馬伸橋，夾林河而下別山鋪，夾陰流河而下至於陰流。

translations.literal: North of Jizhou city, Huangya Camp; west of the city, Baima Spring and Zhenguo Manor; east of the city, Mashen Bridge; following Lin River down to Bieshan Post; following Yinliu River down reaching Yinliu.
translations.idiomatic: North of Jizhou stood Huangya Camp; west of the city, Baima Spring and Zhenguo Manor; east of the city, Mashen Bridge; along the Lin River down to Bieshan Post; along the Yinliu River down to Yinliu.

sentences.zh: 遵化平安城，夾運河而下沙河鋪西，城南鐵廠、湧珠湖以下韭菜溝、上素河、下素河百餘里。

translations.literal: Zunhua's Ping'an city, following the Grand Canal down west of Shahe Post; south of the city, Tiechang and Yongzhu Lake below, down through Jiucai Gully, Upper Su River, and Lower Su River for more than one hundred li.
translations.idiomatic: At Zunhua's Ping'an city, along the Grand Canal west of Shahe Post; south of the city, Tiechang and below Yongzhu Lake through Jiucai Gully, Upper Su River, and Lower Su River for more than one hundred li.

sentences.zh: 豐潤之南，則大寨、剌榆坨、史家河、大王莊，東則榛子鎮，西則鴉紅橋，夾河五十餘里。

translations.literal: South of Fengrun, then Dazhai, Ciyu Tuo, Shijia River, Dawang Manor; east then Zhenzi Town; west then Yahong Bridge; along the river more than fifty li.
translations.idiomatic: South of Fengrun lay Dazhai, Ciyu Tuo, Shijia River, and Dawang Manor; to the east, Zhenzi Town; to the west, Yahong Bridge—more than fifty li along the river.

sentences.zh: 玉田青莊塢、後湖莊、三里屯及大泉、小泉，至於瀕海之地，自水道沽關、黑嚴子墩至開平衛南宋家營，東西百餘里，南北百八十里。

translations.literal: Yutian's Qingzhuangwu, Houhuzhuang, Sanlitun and Great Spring and Little Spring, reaching the coastal lands; from Shuidao Gu Pass and Heiyanzi Mound to Kaiping Guard's Southern Songjiaying in the Song—east-west more than one hundred li, north-south one hundred eighty li.
translations.idiomatic: Yutian's Qingzhuangwu, Houhuzhuang, Sanlitun, and the Great and Little Springs, down to the coast—from Shuidao Gu Pass and Heiyanzi Mound to Kaiping Guard's Southern Songjiaying: more than one hundred li east to west and one hundred eighty li north to south.

sentences.zh: 墾田三萬九千餘畝。

translations.literal: Reclaimed fields more than thirty-nine thousand mu.
translations.idiomatic: They reclaimed more than thirty-nine thousand mu of fields.

sentences.zh: 至真定將治滹沱近堧地，御史王之棟言：「滹沱非人力可治，徒耗財擾民。

translations.literal: Reaching Zhending, about to manage Hutuo near-embankment lands, censor Wang Zhidong said: "Hutuo is not within human power to govern; vainly consuming wealth and disturbing the people.
translations.idiomatic: When he was about to tackle the Hutuo lowlands near Zhending, censor Wang Zhidong argued, "The Hutuo cannot be tamed by human effort; it would only waste money and trouble the people.

sentences.zh: 」帝入其言，欲罪諸建議者。

translations.literal: " The emperor accepted his words and wished to punish those who had proposed the project.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took his view and meant to punish those who had urged the scheme.

sentences.zh: 申時行言：「墾田興利謂之害民，議甚舛。

translations.literal: Shen Shixing said: "Calling land reclamation and public benefit harmful to the people—the argument is very perverse.
translations.idiomatic: Shen Shixing said, "To call land reclamation and public benefit harmful to the people is perverse reasoning.

sentences.zh: 顧為此說者，其故有二。

translations.literal: Those who hold this view have two reasons.
translations.idiomatic: Those who say so have two motives.

sentences.zh: 北方民遊惰好閑，憚於力作，水田有耕耨之勞，胼胝之苦，不便一也。

translations.literal: Northern people are idle and fond of leisure, fearing hard labor; paddy fields have plowing and hoeing toil, callused-hands suffering—inconvenient, one.
translations.idiomatic: First, northerners are lazy and shy from hard work; wet rice demands plowing, hoeing, and blistered hands—they find that inconvenient.

sentences.zh: 貴勢有力家侵佔甚多，不待耕作，坐收蘆葦薪芻之利；

translations.literal: Powerful noble households occupy very much, not waiting to farm but sitting to collect reed, rush, and fodder profits;
translations.idiomatic: Second, powerful families have seized vast tracts and, without farming, simply harvest reeds, rushes, and fodder.

sentences.zh: 若開墾成田，歸於業戶，隸於有司，則已利盡失，不便二也。

translations.literal: If opened and reclaimed into fields, returning to cultivating households and subordinating to officials, then existing profits are wholly lost—inconvenient, two.
translations.idiomatic: If the land were opened into fields, returned to farming households, and placed under officials, those easy profits would vanish.

sentences.zh: 然以國家大計較之，不便者小，而便者大。

translations.literal: Yet measured against the state's great plan, the inconveniences are small and the conveniences great.
translations.idiomatic: Yet weighed against the nation's larger interest, the inconveniences are small and the gains great.

sentences.zh: 惟在斟酌地勢，體察人情，沙堿不必盡開，黍麥無煩改作，應用伕役，必官募之，不拂民情，不失地利，乃謀國長策耳。

translations.literal: Only in weighing terrain, observing human sentiment, sandy alkali need not all be opened, millet and wheat need not be changed over, when employing laborers it must be officially recruited, not going against popular feeling, not losing terrain's advantage—then it is the long strategy for planning the state.
translations.idiomatic: The long strategy is to read the terrain and the people: not every saline plot must be opened, nor every millet field turned to rice; labor should be hired by the state without trampling local custom or wasting the land's strengths.

sentences.zh: 」於是貞明得無罪，而水田事終罷。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Zhenming escaped punishment, but paddy-field work in the end ceased.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenming was spared punishment, but the paddy-field program was abandoned in the end.

sentences.zh: 巡撫都御史樑問孟築橫城堡邊牆，慮寧夏有黃河患，請堤西岔河，障水東流。

translations.literal: Grand coordinator Liang Wenmeng built the Hengcheng Castle border wall and, fearing a Yellow River disaster in Ningxia, requested diking the West Cha River to block water flowing east.
translations.idiomatic: Grand coordinator Liang Wenmeng raised the border wall at Hengcheng Castle and, fearing Yellow River flooding in Ningxia, asked to dike the West Cha River to turn the current eastward.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: It was followed.
translations.idiomatic: The request was approved.

sentences.zh: 十九年，尚寶丞周弘禴言：「寧夏河東有漢、秦二壩，請依河西漢、唐壩築以石，於渠外疏大渠一道，北達鴛鴦諸湖。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year, Junior Chamberlain Zhou Hongzuo said: "East of the Ningxia River are Han and Qin dams; request following the west-bank Han and Tang dams to build in stone, outside the canal opening a great canal one channel, north reaching Mandarin Duck and other lakes.
translations.idiomatic: In year nineteen Junior Chamberlain Zhou Hongzuo reported, "East of the Ningxia River stand the Han and Qin dams; build them in stone like the Han and Tang dams on the west bank, and outside the canal cut a great channel north to Mandarin Duck and the other lakes.

sentences.zh: 」詔可。

translations.literal: " An edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor assented.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，黃、淮漲溢，淮、揚昏墊。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year, the Yellow and Huai rose and overflowed; Huai-Yang were dimmed and submerged.
translations.idiomatic: In year twenty-three the Yellow and Huai flooded; Huai-Yang lay drowned under murky water.

sentences.zh: 議者多請開高家堰以分淮。

translations.literal: Discussants mostly requested opening Gaojia Embankment to divide the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: Most memorialists urged opening Gaojia Embankment to split the Huai.

sentences.zh: 寶應知縣陳煃為御史，慮高堰既開，害民產鹽場，請自興、鹽迤東，疏白塗河、石鵜達口、廖家港為數河，分門出海；

translations.literal: Baoying magistrate Chen Huang, made censor, feared that once Gaojia Embankment was opened it would harm the people's salt fields; requested from Xing and Yan eastward to dredge Baitu River, Shipu Dadao, and Liaojia Harbor as several rivers, dividing gates to reach the sea;
translations.idiomatic: Baoying magistrate Chen Huang, now a censor, feared that opening Gaojia Embankment would ruin the people's salt pans; he asked that east from Xing and Yan the Baitu River, Shipu Dadao, and Liaojia Harbor be cleared as several outlets to the sea;

sentences.zh: 然後從下而上，浚清水、子嬰二溝，且多開瓜、儀閘口以泄水。

translations.literal: then from below upward dredge Qingshui and Ziying two gullies, and moreover open many Guayi sluice mouths to release water.
translations.idiomatic: then, working from downstream upward, clear the Qingshui and Ziying gullies and open more sluices at Guayi to discharge the flood.

sentences.zh: 給事中祝世祿亦言：「議者欲放淮從廣陽、射陽二湖入海。

translations.literal: Supervising secretary Zhu Shilu also said: "Discussants wish to release the Huai from Guangyang and Sheyang two lakes to reach the sea.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising secretary Zhu Shilu also wrote, "Some propose to send the Huai out through Guangyang and Sheyang lakes into the sea.

sentences.zh: 廣陽闊僅八里，射陽僅二十五丈，名為湖，實河也。

translations.literal: Guangyang is only eight li wide; Sheyang only twenty-five zhang—named lakes, in fact rivers.
translations.idiomatic: Guangyang is only eight li across; Sheyang only twenty-five zhang—they are called lakes but are really rivers.

sentences.zh: 且離海三百里，迂迴淺窄，高、寶七州縣水惟此一線宣洩之，又使淮注焉，田廬鹽場，必無幸矣。

translations.literal: Moreover three hundred li from the sea, winding, shallow, and narrow—Gaoyou and Baoying's seven prefectures and counties have only this one line to discharge water; if the Huai is also poured in, fields, houses, and salt pans will surely have no escape.
translations.idiomatic: They lie three hundred li from the sea, winding, shallow, and narrow—the seven prefectures and counties of Gaoyou and Baoying have only this single outlet; pour the Huai into it and fields, homes, and salt pans would be doomed.

sentences.zh: 廣陽湖東有大湖，方廣六十里，湖北口有舊官河，自官蕩至鹽城石鵜達口，通海僅五十三里，此導淮入海一便也。

translations.literal: East of Guangyang Lake is a great lake sixty li square; north of the lake mouth is an old official river, from Guandang to Yancheng's Shipu Dadao, reaching the sea in only fifty-three li—this is one convenience for guiding the Huai to the sea.
translations.idiomatic: East of Guangyang Lake lies a great lake sixty li square; north of its mouth runs an old official channel from Guandang to Yancheng's Shipu Dadao—only fifty-three li to the sea—an easy route for the Huai to reach the ocean.

sentences.zh: 」下部及河漕官議，俱格不行。

translations.literal: " Sent down to ministries and river-transport officials for discussion; all were blocked and not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal went to the ministries and river-transport offices for debate, but every line was blocked and nothing was done.

sentences.zh: 既而總河尚書楊一魁言：「黃水倒灌，正以海口為阻。

translations.literal: Afterward Director-General of Rivers Yang Yikui said: "Yellow water pours back because the estuary is obstructed.
translations.idiomatic: Director-General of Rivers Yang Yikui then argued, "The Yellow River backs up because the estuary is choked.

sentences.zh: 分黃工就，則石鵜達口、廖家港、白駒場海口，金灣、芒稻諸河，急宜開刷。

translations.literal: The work to divide the Yellow being finished, then Shipu Dadao, Liaojia Harbor, Baiju Chang estuary, Jinwan, Mangdao, and other rivers should urgently be opened and scoured.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Yellow River diversion is done, Shipu Dadao, Liaojia Harbor, the Baiju Chang estuary, Jinwan, Mangdao, and the other channels must be opened and scoured at once.

sentences.zh: 」乃命如議行之。

translations.literal: " Thereupon an order was issued to carry it out as discussed.
translations.idiomatic: An order followed to implement the plan.

sentences.zh: 三十年，保定巡撫都御史汪應蛟言：「易水可溉金臺，滹水可溉恆山，溏水可溉中山，滏水可溉襄國，漳水可溉鄴下，而瀛海當眾河下流，故號河中，視江南澤國不異。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year, Baoding grand coordinator Wang Yingjiao said: "Yishui can irrigate Jintai, Hutuo can irrigate Hengshan, Tang can irrigate Zhongshan, Fu can irrigate Xiangguo, Zhang can irrigate below Ye—yet Yinghai lies where all rivers descend downstream, hence called River Center; viewed against Jiangnan's water country it is no different.
translations.idiomatic: In year thirty Baoding grand coordinator Wang Yingjiao wrote, "The Yishui could irrigate Jintai, the Hutuo Hengshan, the Tang Zhongshan, the Fu Xiangguo, the Zhang the lands below Ye—and Yinghai, where every river ends, is called River Center; it is no less a water country than the south.

sentences.zh: 至於山下之泉，地中之水，所在皆有，宜各設壩建閘，通渠築堤，高者自灌，下則車汲。

translations.literal: As for springs on mountainsides and water in the ground, everywhere they exist; each place should set dams and build sluices, open canals and build dikes—high places self-irrigated, low places then cart and draw.
translations.idiomatic: Springs on the hillsides and groundwater below are found everywhere; dams and sluices, canals and dikes should be built so high fields can irrigate themselves and low fields be watered by lift.

sentences.zh: 用南方水田法，六郡之內，得水田數萬頃，畿民從此饒，永無旱澇之患。

translations.literal: Using southern paddy-field methods, within the six prefectures obtaining paddy fields tens of thousands of mu—the capital region's people from this will be abundant, forever without drought and flood disaster.
translations.idiomatic: With southern wet-field methods, tens of thousands of mu of paddy could be gained across the six prefectures; the metropolitan people would grow rich and be forever free of drought and flood.

sentences.zh: 不幸濱河有梗，亦可改折於南，取糴於北。

translations.literal: If unfortunately along the river there is obstruction, grain transport can also be redirected southward, taking grain from the north.
translations.idiomatic: If the river route were blocked, tribute grain could be shifted south and provisions drawn from the north.

sentences.zh: 此國家無窮利也。

translations.literal: This is the state's inexhaustible profit.
translations.idiomatic: That would be profit without end for the state.

sentences.zh: 」報可。

translations.literal: " Reply: approved.
translations.idiomatic: The court approved.

sentences.zh: 應蛟乃於天津葛沽、何家圈、雙溝、白塘，令防海軍丁屯種，人授田四畝，共種五千餘畝，水稻二千畝，收多，因上言：「墾地七千頃，歲可得穀二百餘萬石，此行之而效者也。」

translations.literal: Yingjiao then at Tianjin's Geju, Hejiaquan, Shuanggou, and Baitang ordered coastal-defense troops to garrison and plant; each man four mu of fields, altogether more than five thousand mu planted, paddy two thousand mu—harvest abundant; therefore above said: "Reclaimed land seven thousand qing, yearly can obtain grain more than two million shi—this is what was carried out and took effect."
translations.idiomatic: Yingjiao had coastal-defense troops plant at Tianjin's Geju, Hejiaquan, Shuanggou, and Baitang—four mu per man, more than five thousand mu in all, two thousand mu in rice—with a rich harvest; he reported, "Seven thousand qing reclaimed would yield more than two million shi a year; here is proof the policy works."

sentences.zh: 是年，真定知府郭勉浚大鳴、小鳴泉四十餘穴，溉田千頃。

translations.literal: That year, Zhending prefect Guo Mian dredged Great Ming and Little Ming springs more than forty openings, irrigating fields one thousand qing.
translations.idiomatic: That year Zhending prefect Guo Mian opened more than forty outlets of the Great and Little Ming springs and irrigated one thousand qing of fields.

sentences.zh: 邢臺達活、野狐二泉流為牛尾河，百泉流為澧河，建二十一閘二堤，灌田五百餘頃。

translations.literal: Xingtai's Dahu and Yehu two springs flowed into Niwei River; the Hundred Springs flowed into Li River; twenty-one sluices and two dikes were built, irrigating fields more than five hundred qing.
translations.idiomatic: At Xingtai the Dahu and Yehu springs fed the Niwei River and the Hundred Springs the Li River; twenty-one sluices and two dikes were built to water more than five hundred qing.

sentences.zh: 天啟元年，御史左光鬥用應蛟策，復天津屯田，令通判盧觀象管理屯田水利。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianqi, censor Zuo Guangdou used Yingjiao's plan, restored Tianjin garrison fields, and ordered vice prefect Lu Guanxiang to manage garrison-field water conservancy.
translations.idiomatic: In Tianqi year one censor Zuo Guangdou revived Yingjiao's scheme, restored Tianjin garrison fields, and put vice prefect Lu Guanxiang in charge of their irrigation.

sentences.zh: 明年，巡按御史張慎言言：「自枝河而西，靜海、興濟之間，萬頃沃壤。

translations.literal: The next year, investigating censor Zhang Shenyan said: "West of the branch river, between Jinghai and Xingji, ten thousand qing of fertile soil.
translations.idiomatic: The next year investigating censor Zhang Shenyan wrote, "West of the branch channel, between Jinghai and Xingji, lies ten thousand qing of rich soil.

sentences.zh: 河之東，尚有鹽水沽等處為膏腴之田，惜皆蕪廢。

translations.literal: East of the river, Yanshui Gu and other places still have fertile fields—alas all lie waste.
translations.idiomatic: East of the river, Yanshui Gu and the like remain fertile ground—yet all lie abandoned.

sentences.zh: 今觀象開寇家口以南田三千餘畝，溝洫蘆塘之法，種植疏浚之方，皆具而有法，人何憚而不為？

translations.literal: Now Guanxiang has opened more than three thousand mu of fields south of Koujiakou; methods for ditches, reed ponds, planting, and dredging are all complete and regulated—why should people fear and not act?
translations.idiomatic: Guanxiang has already opened more than three thousand mu south of Koujiakou with full methods for ditches, reed ponds, planting, and dredging—what keeps people from following suit?

sentences.zh: 大抵開種之法有五：一官種。

translations.literal: In general the methods for opening cultivation are five: first, official planting.
translations.idiomatic: Opening land, in brief, follows five methods. First, official planting.

sentences.zh: 謂牛、種、器具、耕作、僱募皆出於官，而官亦盡收其田之入也。

translations.literal: Meaning oxen, seed, tools, plowing, and hired labor all come from the government, and the government also fully collects the fields' yield.
translations.idiomatic: The state supplies oxen, seed, tools, plowing, and hired labor and takes the entire harvest.

sentences.zh: 一佃種。

translations.literal: Second, tenant planting.
translations.idiomatic: Second, tenant planting.

sentences.zh: 謂民願墾而無力，其牛、種、器具仰給於官，待納稼之時，官十而取其四也。

translations.literal: Meaning the people wish to reclaim but lack strength; their oxen, seed, and tools rely on the government; when grain is delivered, the government takes four parts in ten.
translations.idiomatic: Peasants who wish to reclaim but lack means receive oxen, seed, and tools from the state and pay four-tenths of the harvest at harvest time.

sentences.zh: 一民種。

translations.literal: Third, civilian planting.
translations.idiomatic: Third, civilian planting.

sentences.zh: 佃之有力者，自認開墾若干，迨開荒既熟，較數歲之中以為常，十一而取是也。

translations.literal: Tenants with means themselves acknowledge opening a set amount; when wasteland is already ripe, comparing several years' yield as the norm, one in ten is taken.
translations.idiomatic: Stronger tenants pledge to open a set acreage; once the wasteland bears, a tithe is taken based on several years' average yield.

sentences.zh: 一軍種。

translations.literal: Fourth, military planting.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth, military planting.

sentences.zh: 即令海防營軍種葛沽之田，人耕四畝，收二石，緣有行、月糧，故收租重也。

translations.literal: That is, ordering coastal-defense troops to plant Geju fields—each man cultivates four mu, harvest two shi; because they have travel and monthly rations, therefore rent collection is heavy.
translations.idiomatic: Coastal-defense troops plant the Geju fields—four mu per man, two shi harvested—and because they still draw travel pay and monthly grain, the rent is heavier.

sentences.zh: 一屯種。

translations.literal: Fifth, garrison planting.
translations.idiomatic: Fifth, garrison planting.

sentences.zh: 祖宗衛軍有屯田，或五十畝，或百畝。

translations.literal: Ancestral guard troops had garrison fields, either fifty mu or one hundred mu.
translations.idiomatic: The founding guard troops held garrison fields of fifty or one hundred mu each.

sentences.zh: 軍為屯種者，歲入十七於官，即以所入為官軍歲支之用。

translations.literal: Soldiers who garrison-planted yearly delivered seventeen parts to the government, and with what was delivered supplied the official troops' yearly disbursements.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers on garrison duty paid seventeen parts of the yield to the state, which funded the troops' annual pay.

sentences.zh: 國初兵農之善制也。

translations.literal: The founding era's excellent system joining army and agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: It was the founding era's fine union of army and agriculture.

sentences.zh: 四法已行，惟屯種則今日兵與軍分，而屯僅存其名。

translations.literal: The four methods are already in practice; only garrison planting—today soldiers and troops are divided, and garrison exists in name only.
translations.idiomatic: Four of these methods are already in use; only garrison planting survives in name, for soldiers and garrison troops are now separate.

sentences.zh: 當選各衛之屯餘，墾津門之沃土，如官種法行之。

translations.literal: The various guards' surplus garrison lands should be selected, reclaiming Tianjin's fertile soil, carried out like official planting.
translations.idiomatic: Surplus garrison land from the guards should be chosen to reclaim Tianjin's rich soil under the official-planting method.

sentences.zh: 」章下所司，命太僕卿董應舉管天津至山海屯田，規畫數年，開田十八萬畝，積穀無算。

translations.literal: " The memorial was sent to the responsible offices; the emperor ordered Grand Steward Dong Yingju to oversee garrison fields from Tianjin to Shanhai, planning several years, opening fields one hundred eighty thousand mu, accumulated grain beyond reckoning.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial went to the responsible offices; the emperor ordered Grand Steward Dong Yingju to oversee garrison fields from Tianjin to Shanhai. Over several years he opened one hundred eighty thousand mu and amassed grain beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 崇禎二年，兵部侍郎申用懋言：「永平濼河諸水，逶迤寬衍，可疏渠以防旱潦。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chongzhen, Vice Minister of War Shen Yongmao said: "Yongping's Luo River and various waters wind far and spread wide; channels can be dredged to guard against drought and flood.
translations.idiomatic: In Chongzhen year two Vice Minister of War Shen Yongmao wrote, "The Luo River and other streams of Yongping wind wide and far; canals could be cut to guard against drought and flood.

sentences.zh: 山坡隙地，便栽種。

translations.literal: Hillside gaps in the land are convenient for planting.
translations.idiomatic: Slopes and pockets of ground are fit for planting.

sentences.zh: 宜令有司相地察源，為民興利。

translations.literal: It is fitting to order the responsible offices to survey the land and inspect sources, promoting benefit for the people.
translations.idiomatic: Officials should be ordered to survey the terrain, trace the water sources, and bring the people real benefit.
